# Orchestrator reviews implementation

Load when a request involves any of these terms: review, diff, approve, review findings.

## Step instructions

Inspect the REAL diff, never a self-reported summary: `git diff`, or read the
files at the WorkNode's target. Judge whether it matches the description and
intent, stays in scope, and that any test failure
you surfaced is handled here rather than left to the user.

FIX, don't flag, when the defect is minor — a stale assertion, a wrong import, a
failing test you can correct. Re-run the narrow tests, then approve. Leave
orchestrator_approved false when it is NOT minor: the run bounces back to
implement instead of you quietly becoming the implementer.

Re-check this work's linked designs against the real diff before approving --
`cwpilot play show {RUN_ID} --source -v` or `cwpilot work explain <id>` re-renders
them. They rendered once at initial dispatch, but this is the point where the real
diff exists to compare against: a design that was current then may already be
stale or contradicted by what actually got built. This is review's job, not
commit's — commit only records a decision already made.

Record facts.orchestrator_approved and facts.review_findings — which criteria you
checked and what you found, not a restatement of the verdict.

## Facts

- `orchestrator_approved`: Whether the changes pass review.
- `rejection_reason`: Why the changes were rejected, when orchestrator_approved is false.
- `review_findings`: Prose record of what was checked during review and what was found -- the evidence behind the verdict, not the verdict itself. Required when approving (orchestrator_approved is true). Persisted on the WorkNode in the generic StepEvidence record.
